newsitem.title: CONGO: Rebels in Angola enclave seize Asian workers.
newsitem.headline: Rebels in Angola enclave seize Asian workers.

text.p: An armed group fighting for independence in Angola's oil-rich Cabinda enclave said on Monday it had taken prisoner two Asian engineers who would face trial on charges of spying for the Angolan authorities.

A spokesman for the armed wing of the Front for the Liberation of the Cabinda Enclave (FLEC-FAC) said the two -- a Malaysian and a Filipino working with Malaysian timber company INWANGSA-SDN -- would be executed or expelled.

Emmanuel N'Zita, son of FLEC-FAC leader Henriques Tiago N'Zita, who lives in France, said Omar Bin Norola, 46, from Malaysia, and Marcellin Alime, 50, from the Philippines, had been captured on Saturday.

"These two expatriates were infiltrated into this timber company by the Angolan government to undertake reconnaissance in the zone controlled by FLEC-FAC," Emmanuel N'Zita told a news conference in Congo's capital Brazzaville.
They would tried under "revolutionary law" in force in the zone, he said, adding that this envisaged expulsion or execution.
Last weekend FLEC-FAC warned foreign investors to leave Cabinda immediately as it planned to attack Angolan and foreign economic targets there.
About 20 timber companies work there, mostly Portuguese, plus oil companies such as Chevron, ELF, AGIP and Angola's SONAGOL.
Cabinda, a former Portuguese protectorate, became an Angolan province in 1975.
